sections.h2: Who bills and collects property tax in Syracuse
sections.html:
One office, the City Payment Center, prepares the bill and takes payment for City, School and County property tax together. The Department of Assessment sets the value. Both are in City Hall at 233 East Washington Street. The Payment Center is in Room 122, open Monday to Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., and its phone is 315-448-8310. Assessment is in Suite 130 at 315-448-8270.

The Payment Center services more than 42,000 taxpayer accounts. It also chases delinquent property tax and handles the sale of tax-delinquent properties. Use the Market Street entrance to City Hall, plan on a security check, and expect metered parking on nearby streets.

  • Payment Center: bills, payments, delinquent tax, tax trust payment plans.
  • Assessment: values, exemptions, change of address for notices, grievance forms.
  • Onondaga County Clerk: copies of deeds.

Due dates are printed on your bill. If you need them for the current year, call the City Payment Center at 315-448-8310. The same office can tell you what you owe today and whether any prior year is open. A tax question that reaches the Assessment office gets routed to the Payment Center anyway.

If bills are going to the wrong place, file a Change of Address for City Service Notifications with the Department of Assessment. The form covers tax bills, assessment notices and other property mail. Owners who have moved away or inherited a house should file it before the next bill cycle.

Homeowners who have fallen behind can apply for a tax trust, the City's payment plan for delinquent property tax. The application is a PDF on the Payment Center page. Parcels that go through tax foreclosure are transferred to the Greater Syracuse Property Development Corporation, known as the Land Bank, and are then offered for sale there.

When you visit the Payment Center, bring your bill or the parcel address, a photo ID, and any letter you received about a past-due balance. Ask for a printout of what is owed and what has been paid, so you can hand it to your closing attorney. If you are applying for a tax trust, ask what the first payment must be before you leave.

sections.h2: How to challenge your Syracuse assessment
sections.html:
File a formal grievance with the Board of Assessment Review during the last two weeks of January. The board has four or five officers appointed by the City Council, and it can lower an assessment for good cause. Grounds include an assessment that is unequal, excessive or unlawful, and a wrong property classification.

Fill out the grievance form, print it and sign it by hand. Bring or mail it to City Hall, Suite 130. The office takes only forms with an original signature, complete documentation, and a filing date inside those two weeks. Forms that arrive early or late are not taken. Evening and Saturday-morning hours have been posted during the window.

State law requires every property to be held at a uniform percentage of market value (RPTL sections 301 and 305). Syracuse values by cost, income and comparable sales, then adjusts for physical changes or market shifts. Each parcel has its own market value, which is why neighbors' assessments differ. Gather recent sales of similar houses before you file.

sections.h2: Why your Syracuse tax bill went up
sections.html:
A bill rises when the assessment changes, an exemption status changes, the tax rate moves, or a special charge not tied to assessment is added or increased. If a charge on your bill is unfamiliar, call 315-448-8270 and staff will look into it.

Changes to the building count too. Adding or tearing down a porch or garage can move an assessment to match the new value.

To find out who owns a parcel, the Department points to the SDG Image Mate lookup by address. It keeps no owner phone numbers. The City also keeps tax maps that show lot dimensions but not buildings, so a boundary question needs a private survey from the seller's files.

Most exemptions need an application to the Department of Assessment before January 1. The Department asks you to call or visit instead of downloading a form blind, because each exemption has its own form and supporting papers.

A property cannot take both the senior and the disability exemption on one account. Renewal forms for the income-based programs are mailed each August and must be back before January 1. The Department also offers a historic property exemption and property improvement exemptions for renovating vacant, residential and commercial buildings.

sections.h2: Selling a Syracuse house with tax owing
sections.html:
Get a written payoff from the City Payment Center and ask whether the County and School portions are included. The Payment Center collects all three, so one figure should cover them. Then confirm with your closing attorney that any tax trust balance is paid off at the closing table.

  • Ask the Payment Center whether the account is in a tax trust and what remains owing.
  • Get a copy of your deed from the Onondaga County Clerk, which keeps the official deed records.
  • Check the City's tax map of your parcel. It shows lot lines but not buildings, so a seller usually supplies a private survey.
  • If the exemption on your bill is a senior or disability exemption, tell the buyer it will not carry over.

A cash sale skips the lender's underwriting, but the tax payoff still comes from the sale proceeds. Ask for the payoff early, since the figure changes with the closing date.

Syracuse is a city of renters. The owner-occupancy rate for 2020-2024 is 41.6 percent, the median owner-occupied value is $138,400 and median gross rent is $1,039. Median household income is $47,819. The 2020 census counted 148,620 people, and the July 2025 estimate is 144,896.

With values at that level, a tax bill that is high for the neighborhood can weigh on a sale. If you think your assessment is out of line, the January grievance window is the time to act, and a listing in the spring means you may already have missed it.

faqs.q: Where do I pay my Syracuse property tax?
faqs.a: At the City Payment Center, Room 122 in City Hall, 233 East Washington Street, Monday to Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. It collects City, School and County tax in one place.

faqs.q: When is grievance filing season in Syracuse?
faqs.a: The last two weeks of January each year. The forms must be signed in ink and delivered to City Hall, Suite 130, inside that window.

faqs.q: Can I get a payment plan for back taxes in Syracuse?
faqs.a: Yes. The City Payment Center offers a tax trust for homeowners who have fallen behind. Pick up the application from the Payment Center page or call 315-448-8310.

faqs.q: Does the STAR credit lower a Syracuse bill directly?
faqs.a: Only for owners registered before 2015. Newer registrants get a credit check or direct deposit from New York State, which they use to pay City and School tax.

faqs.q: What happens to a Syracuse house after tax foreclosure?
faqs.a: It is transferred to the Greater Syracuse Property Development Corporation, the Land Bank, which lists available properties for sale.
